"There is no water in the cistern if it does not rise, with a rope over the great pulley (al-mihal al-nughad)."

Al-Mihal and al-Mihalah: the great pulley by which camels are watered.

(And they say: When is it?) That is, the resurrection and the restoration, and this time.

(Say: It may be that it is near.) That is, it is near, because "ʿasa" and "ahabba" (in such contexts denote certainty). Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [see vol. 14, p. 284], and ﴿The Hour is perhaps near﴾ [see vol. 16, p. 15]. And everything that is to come is near.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 52:**

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿On the Day He calls you, and you respond with His praise﴾. The *du'a'* (calling) is the summons to the place of gathering with a speech that all creation hears, through which Allah Exalted calls them to come out. It was also said: it is the Blast that they hear, which summons them to assemble in the land of the Resurrection. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and your fathers' names, so make your names good."

﴿And you respond with His praise﴾: that is, by deserving praise for the giving of life.

Abu Sahl said: that is, "and praise belongs to Allah," as he said:

*"Indeed, by the praise of Allah, I have not worn the garment of a wicked person, nor have I covered myself with a treacherous betrayal."*

It was also said: "He is praised by your tongues." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the disbelievers will come out of their graves saying, "Glory be to You and praise be to You," but that acknowledgment will not benefit them on that Day. Ibn 'Abbas [[In manuscript J: and Sufyan.]] said: "with His praise" means "by His command," i.e., you will acknowledge that He is your Creator. Qatadah said: "by knowing Him and obeying Him." It was also said: the meaning is "by His power." And it was said: "by His calling you." Our scholars said: this is the correct view, for the blowing into the Trumpet is only the cause of the dead coming out of their graves; in reality, the emergence of creation is by the call of the Truth. Allah Exalted said: ﴿On the Day He calls you, and you respond with His praise﴾, and so they stand up saying, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You." He said: the Day of Resurrection is a day that begins with praise and ends with it. Allah Exalted said: ﴿On the Day He calls you, and you respond with His praise﴾, and He said elsewhere: ﴿And judgment will be made between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [[See vol. 15, p. 284 and p. 39.]]

﴿And you will think that you remained only a little﴾: that is, between the two Blasts. The punishment is withheld from the tormented between the two Blasts, and that is forty years, so they sleep. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"Who has raised us from our sleeping place?"﴾ [[See vol. 15, p. 284 and p. 39.]] Thus it is specific to the disbelievers. Mujahid said: the disbelievers have a brief slumber before the Day of Resurrection, in which they find the taste of sleep; then when the people of the graves are called, they rise in fright. Qatadah said: the meaning is that the world shrank in their eyes and seemed small when they saw the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: ﴿And you will think that you remained only a little﴾ refers to the world, because of the length of your stay in the Hereafter.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And tell My servants to say that which is best﴾. Its i'rab (grammatical analysis) has already been discussed [[see vol. 9, p. 366.]]. The verse was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. A man from the Arabs insulted him, so 'Umar reviled him and resolved to kill him, and this almost stirred up strife. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning it: "And tell My servants to say that which is best." This is related by al-Tha'labi, al-Mawardi, Ibn 'Atiyyah and al-Wahidi.

It was also said: it was revealed when the Muslims said, "Grant us permission, O Messenger of Allah, to fight them, for their harm to us has lasted long." He said, "I have not yet been commanded to fight." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "And tell My servants to say that which is best." This was said by al-Kalbi.

It was also said: the meaning is, "Tell My servants, who acknowledge that I am their Creator while they worship idols, to say that which is best, namely the word of tawhid (divine oneness) and the affirmation of prophethood."

It was also said: the meaning is, "And tell My servants, the believers, when they dispute with the disbelievers about tawhid, to say the word that is best," just as He said: ﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾ [[see vol. 7, pp. 60 and 347.]].

Al-Hasan said: it is that one says to the disbeliever, when he oversteps the bounds: "May Allah guide you! May Allah have mercy on you!" And this was before they were commanded to engage in jihad.

It was also said: the meaning is, "Tell them to enjoin what Allah has commanded and forbid what Allah has forbidden." On this view the verse is general, applying to both the believer and the disbeliever; that is, "Say it to everyone." And Allah knows best.

A group said: in this verse Allah, the Exalted, commanded the believers specifically in their dealings among themselves, to observe good manners, speak gently, lower the wing (of humility), and cast aside the promptings of Satan. The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "And be, O servants of Allah, brothers." This is the best view, and the verse is then muhkam (decisive, not abrogated; a term meaning a verse whose ruling is fixed).

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan incites discord among them﴾, that is, by corruption, sowing enmity, and misleading. This has already been discussed at the end of al-A'raf [[see vol. 7, pp. 60 and 347.]] and in Yusuf [[see vol. 9, p. 267.]]. It is said: "Nazagha baynana" meaning "he caused corruption between us." This was stated by al-Yazidi. Others said: al-nazgh means incitement.

﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been to mankind a manifest enemy﴾, that is, of extreme enmity. This has already been discussed in al-Baqarah [[see vol. 2, p. 209.]]. And in a report: "A group of people sat remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Satan came to break up their gathering, but the angels prevented him. He then came to a group sitting near them who were not remembering Allah, and he stirred up discord between them, so they quarrelled and attacked one another. Those who remembered Allah said, 'Come, let us reconcile our brothers.' So they rose and broke up their gathering, and Satan rejoiced at that." This is an example of some of his enmity.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 54:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you.﴾ This is addressed to the polytheists. The meaning is: if He wills, He will guide you to Islam and so have mercy upon you, or He will cause you to die in shirk and so punish you. This was said by Ibn Jurayj. "A'lam" (knows best) here means "'alim" (knowing), like the saying "Allah is Akbar," meaning "Kabir" (Great). It was also said: the address is to the believers, i.e., if He wills, He will have mercy upon you by protecting you from the disbelievers of Makkah, or if He wills, He will punish you by giving them power over you. This was said by al-Kalbi.

(﴿And We did not send you as a guardian over them.﴾) That is, We did not appoint you to prevent them from disbelief, nor did We make their faith your responsibility. It was also said: We did not make you a surety for them, for which you would be held accountable, and this was said by al-Kalbi. The poet said:

I remembered Abu Arwa, so I spent the night as if I were
Responsible (wakil) for returning the past affairs.

That is, a guarantor (kafil).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: "And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others" (﴿وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَلَقَدْ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَ النَّبِيِّينَ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾). He repeats, after saying "Your Lord knows best about you" (﴿رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ﴾), in order to make clear that He is their Creator, that He made them differing in their characters, their forms, their conditions and their wealth: "Should not He who created know?" (﴿أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ﴾) [see vol. 18, p. 213]. Likewise the prophets, some of them were preferred over others, with knowledge from Him of their condition. This matter has already been discussed in al-Baqarah [see vol. 3, p. 261 onwards].

(﴿وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُدَ زَبُورًا﴾) The Zabur (Psalms): a book containing no lawful or unlawful matters, no obligatory duties and no prescribed punishments; it is only supplication, glorification and exaltation. That is, just as We gave Dawud the Zabur, do not deny that Muhammad should be given the Qur'an. And this is in the context of the argument with the Jews.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him﴾. When the Quraysh were afflicted with drought and complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah revealed this verse. That is: call upon those whom you worship besides Him and whom you claim to be gods.

Al-Hasan said: it refers to the angels, ʿIsa, and ʿUzayr. Ibn Masʿud said: it refers to the jinn.

﴿Then they have no power to remove the harm from you﴾, that is, the drought for seven years, according to the view of Muqatil.

﴿Nor to effect any change﴾, from poverty to wealth and from sickness to health.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those whom they call upon﴾. "Ulaika" (those) is a subject (mubtada'), "alladhina" (who) is a qualifier (sifah) of "ulaika," and the relative pronoun (damir al-silah) is omitted, meaning "yad'unahum" (whom they call upon). That is, "ulaika" are those who are being called upon. And "yabtaghun" is the predicate (khabar), or it may be a circumstantial clause (hal), and "alladhina yad'un" is the predicate, meaning: they call upon [ibad or ibadah [[from ms. J and W.]]] to His worship. Ibn Mas'ud read "tad'un" with the ta' as direct address (al-khitab). The rest read it with the ya' as third-person narration (al-khabar). There is no disagreement that "yabtaghun" is with the ya'. In Sahih Muslim, in the Book of Tafsir, it is reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud concerning His saying, may He be mighty and majestic: "Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord," that he said: "A group of jinn who had embraced Islam, and they used to be worshipped, and those who used to worship them remained upon their worship, while that group of jinn had embraced Islam." In another narration he said: It was revealed concerning a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of jinn, then the jinn embraced Islam, while the humans who used to worship them did not realize it, so it was revealed: "Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord." And also from him: they are the angels, whom some tribes of the Arabs used to worship; this was mentioned by al-Mawardi. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Uzayr and Isa.

"Yabtaghun" means they seek from Allah nearness and closeness, and they humble themselves before Allah, may He be exalted, in seeking Paradise, which is the means of access (al-wasilah). Allah, may He be exalted, informed them that the ones worshipped seek closeness to their Lord. The ha' and mim in "rabbihim" refer to the worshippers, or to the worshipped, or to both of them together. As for "yad'un," it refers to the worshippers, and "yabtaghun" refers to the worshipped.

(Ayyuhum aqrab) is an inceptive subject and predicate (mubtada' wa khabar). It is also permissible for "ayyuhum aqrab" to be a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "yabtaghun," and the meaning is: whichever of them is nearest seeks the means of access to Allah.

(And they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment; indeed the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared) meaning, a thing to be dreaded, not a thing that anyone is safe from, so one should beware of it and fear it. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Hope and fear are two scales for a person; when they are balanced, his states are upright, and if one of them outweighs the other, the other is nullified.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is no town but We will destroy it﴾ before the Day of Resurrection, i.e., We will ruin it (mukhribuha).

(Or punish it with a severe punishment.) Muqatil said: As for the righteous town, it is by death; as for the wicked town, it is by punishment. Ibn Mas'ud said: When adultery (al-zina) and usury (al-riba) become widespread in a town, Allah permits its destruction. It was said: the meaning is "And there is no wicked town," and this is strengthened by His saying: ﴿And We never destroyed a town except that its people were wrongdoers﴾ [see vol. 13, p. 301]. That is, let the polytheists beware, for there is no disbelieving town but that punishment will descend upon it.

(That was in the Book) i.e., in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh).

(Inscribed) i.e., written. Al-satr (al-satr): the line, the writing; it is originally a verbal noun. Al-satar (with a vowel on the second letter) is similar to it. Jarir said:

Whoever wishes, I will sell him my wealth and my choice possessions... what the Taym's ledgers [in Jarir's Diwan: "what the Khalaj complete"] of their registers contain of lines (satran).

Al-khul'ah (with a dammah on the kha'): the choicest of wealth. The plural of satr is asfar (asfar), like sabab and asbab, and then it is pluralized as asatir (asatir). The plural of al-satr is ustur and sutur, like fils and fulus. Here al-kitab is intended to mean the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not withhold from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾. In the speech there is an ellipsis (ḥadhf), and the implied meaning is: "And We did not withhold from sending the signs they asked for, except that they would deny them and so be destroyed, as was done to those before them." This is the explanation given by Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and others. So Allah delayed the punishment from the disbelievers of Quraysh because He knew that among them there would be those who believe and among them those who would be born believers. It has already been mentioned in al-An'am [[See vol. 6, p. 387.]] and elsewhere that they asked that Allah turn Safa into gold for them and move the mountains away from them, and Gabriel descended and said: "If you wish, what your people asked will happen; but if they do not believe, they will not be given respite. And if you wish, I will delay them." He said: "No, rather, delay them."

The first "an" (that) is in the accusative position, as the object of the negation falling upon them, and the second "an" is in the nominative position. The "ba'" in "bil-ayat" is extra (zā'idah). The figurative sense of the statement is: "And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except the denial of the former peoples." Allah the Exalted cannot be prevented from anything, so the meaning is an emphasis that He does not do it, as though He had been prevented from it.

Then He explained what He did to those who asked for signs and did not believe in them, saying: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, meaning a clear, illuminating, radiant sign indicating the truthfulness of Salih and the power of Allah the Exalted. This has been mentioned before [[See vol. 7, p. 238 and vol. 9, p. 60.]].

﴿But they wronged themselves by it﴾, meaning they wronged themselves by denying it. It is also said: they rejected it and disbelieved that it was from Allah, so Allah uprooted them with punishment.

﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾. Regarding this there are five opinions. The first: the lessons and the miracles which Allah placed at the hands of the messengers are among the proofs of warning, a means of frightening the deniers. The second: they are signs of retribution, frightening people away from sins. The third: they are the changing of conditions from childhood to youth, then to maturity, then to gray hair, so that you may take heed from the changing of your own conditions and fear the outcome of your affair; this is the view of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him. The fourth: the Qur'an. The fifth: sudden plague (al-mawt al-dhari'), said by al-Hasan [[That is, the swift, widespread death by which people hardly have time to bury one another.]].

**Verse 17:60:** ﴿And [remember] when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "The people here are the people of Makkah, and His encompassing them is His destroying them, meaning that Allah will destroy them." He mentioned it in the past tense to affirm that it will certainly happen. By this promised destruction he meant what took place at Badr and on the Day of the Conquest (of Makkah). It was also said: the meaning of "encompassed the people" is that His power surrounds them, so they are in His grasp and cannot escape His will. This was said by Mujahid and Ibn Abi Najih. Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is that His knowledge encompasses the people. It was also said: the intended meaning is His protecting you from the people, so that they do not kill you until you convey the message of your Lord. That is, "We did not send you as a guardian over them; rather, your duty is to convey (the message). So convey it earnestly, for We will protect you from them and safeguard you. Do not be intimidated by them, and proceed with what I command you of conveying the message, for Our power encompasses everything." This was the view of al-Hasan, 'Urwah, Qatadah and others.

**Verse 17:60 (continued):** ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾. When (Allah) explained that the revelation of the verses of the Qur'an contains a warning, He added to it the mention of the verse of the Night Journey (al-Isra'), which is mentioned at the beginning of the surah. In al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, "And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people," he said: "It is the vision of sight which the Prophet (ﷺ) was shown on the night he was taken by night (isra') to Bayt al-Maqdis." He said: "And the accursed tree in the Qur'an" is the tree of al-Zaqqum (a bitter tree in Hell). Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sound hadith." The view of Ibn 'Abbas was also held by 'A'ishah, Mu'awiyah, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Abi Najih and Ibn Zayd. The trial was the apostasy of some people who had embraced Islam when the Prophet (ﷺ) informed them that he had been taken by night. It was also said: it was a dream during sleep. This verse refutes that view, because there is no trial in a dream, and no one would deny it. From Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "The vision in this verse is the vision of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he would enter Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. He was turned back, so the Muslims were tested by it, and the verse was revealed. When the following year came, he entered it, and Allah the Exalted revealed: 'Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision with truth'" [[See vol. 16, p. 289.]]. But this interpretation is weak, because the surah is Meccan, and that vision was in Madinah. In a third report it is said: the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in a dream the Banu Marwan climbing on his pulpit like monkeys, which distressed him. It was said to him: "It is only the worldly life that has been given to them," and so he was relieved. He had no pulpit in Makkah, but it is possible that he saw in Makkah a vision of the pulpit in Madinah. This third interpretation was also given by Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him. Sahl said: "This vision was only that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the Banu Umayyah climbing on his pulpit like monkeys, and he was saddened by it, and from that day he was never seen laughing until he died (ﷺ)." So the verse was revealed informing that this was from their gaining power and rising (to positions), which Allah makes a trial and a test for the people. Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, in his sermon concerning his giving of allegiance to Mu'awiyah, recited: "And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time" [[See vol. 11, p. 350.]]. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "There is room for scrutiny in this interpretation, and 'Uthman, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and Mu'awiyah are not included in this vision."

**Verse 17:60 (continued):** ﴿And the accursed tree in the Qur'an﴾. There is an inversion in the wording, meaning: "We did not make the vision which We showed you and the accursed tree in the Qur'an except as a trial for the people." Its trial was that when they were warned by it, Abu Jahl said mockingly: "This Muhammad threatens you with a fire that burns stones, then he claims that it produces trees, while fire consumes trees. We do not know al-Zaqqum except as dates and butter." Then Abu Jahl ordered a slave girl, who brought dates and butter, and he said to his companions: "Eat zaqqum." It has been said that the one who said "We do not know al-Zaqqum except as dates and butter" was Ibn al-Zib'ara, when he said: "May Allah multiply al-Zaqqum in your house, for it is dates with butter in the dialect of Yemen." It is possible that both of them said it. Some of the weak in faith were also tested by this statement, so Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He had made the Night Journey and the mention of the tree of al-Zaqqum a trial and a test, so that whoever was already destined for disbelief would disbelieve, and whoever was already destined for faith would believe. As it is narrated that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was told on the morning after the Night Journey: "Your companion claims that he went last night to Bayt al-Maqdis." He said: "If he said that, then he has spoken the truth." It was said to him: "Do you affirm it before you hear it from him?" He said: "Woe to your minds! I affirm him regarding news of the heaven, so how should I not affirm him regarding news of Bayt al-Maqdis, when the heaven is far more distant than it?"

**I say:** Ibn Ishaq narrated this report, and its text is: He said: "Among the accounts which reached me concerning his night journey (ﷺ), from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, 'A'ishah, Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Qatadah and others of the people of knowledge, and Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, none of them gathered all of this hadith; each one narrated to me some of what was mentioned about his affair when he was taken by night (ﷺ). His night journey and what was related about it was a trial, a purification, and a matter from the affairs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, concerning His power and authority; in it is a lesson for people of understanding, a guidance, a mercy, and a steadfastness for those who believed and affirmed, and who held to the affair of Allah the Exalted with certainty. So he was taken by night (ﷺ) as He willed and in the manner He willed, so that He might show him of His signs what He wished, until he witnessed what he witnessed of His affair, His great authority, and His power by which He does what He wills." 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, as it reached me from him, used to say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought the Buraq, which is the animal upon which the prophets before him were carried, placing its hoof at the farthest point of its sight. He was mounted upon it, then his companion (Jibril) took him out, showing him the signs between heaven and earth, until he reached Bayt al-Maqdis, where he found Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa, along with a group of the prophets who had been gathered for him. He led them in prayer. Then three vessels were brought to him: a vessel containing milk, a vessel containing wine, and a vessel containing water." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I heard a speaker saying, when they were presented to me: if he takes the water, he will drown and his nation will drown; if he takes the wine, he will go astray and his nation will go astray; and if he takes the milk, he will be guided and his nation will be guided. So I took the vessel of milk and drank it. Jibril said to me: 'You have been guided, and your nation has been guided, O Muhammad.'" Ibn Ishaq said: "I was told from al-Hasan that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'While I was sleeping in al-Hijr, Jibril, peace be upon him, came to me and nudged me with his foot, so I sat up but saw nothing, then I returned to my bed. He came a second time and nudged me with his foot, so I sat up but saw nothing, and I returned to my bed. He came a third time and nudged me with his foot, so I sat up, and he took me by my arms, and I rose with him. He went out to the door of the mosque, and there was a white animal between a mule and a donkey, with two wings on its thighs, with which it moved its legs, placing its hoof at the farthest point of its sight. He carried me upon it, then went out with me, neither outpacing me nor being outpaced by me.'"

Ibn Ishaq said: "I was told from Qatadah that he said: 'I was told that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: When I drew near to it to mount it, it shied away [[Shammasa al-dabbah wa al-faras tashmus: it fled, bolted, and refused to let its back be ridden.]], so Jibril placed his hand upon its mane and said: "Are you not ashamed, O Buraq, of what you are doing? By Allah, no servant of Allah has ever ridden you before Muhammad who is more honored by Him than he is." So it felt shame until it sweated profusely, then it settled down until I mounted it.'" Al-Hasan, in his narration, said: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proceeded, and Jibril proceeded with him, until he reached Bayt al-Maqdis, where he found Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa among a group of the prophets. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led them in prayer. Then two vessels were brought to him: in one was wine and in the other was milk. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the vessel of milk and drank from it, and he left the vessel of wine. Jibril said to him: 'You have been guided to the natural disposition (fitrah), and your nation has been guided, and wine has been forbidden to you.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Makkah. When morning came, he went out to the Quraysh and informed them of the report. Most of the people said: "By Allah, this is a clear matter! By Allah, a caravan takes a month from Makkah to Syria, a month going and a month returning, yet Muhammad claims to have covered it in a single night and returned to Makkah!" He said: "Many who had embraced Islam apostatized. The people went to Abu Bakr and said: 'Do you have any idea, O Abu Bakr, about your companion? He claims that he came last night to Bayt al-Maqdis, prayed there, and returned to Makkah.'" He said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "You are lying about him." They said: "Yes, indeed, he is there in the mosque telling the people about it." Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, if he said it, then he has spoken the truth. Why does this amaze you? By Allah, he informs me that news reaches him from the heaven to the earth in an hour of night or day, and I affirm him; so this is farther than what you find amazing." Then he went until he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you tell these people that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis this night?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, describe it to me, for I have been there." Al-Hasan said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was raised up for me until I looked at it," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began describing it to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "You have spoken the truth. I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." Every time he described some part of it to him, he said: "You have spoken the truth. I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." He said: Until when he finished, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: "And you, O Abu Bakr, are the Siddiq." On that day he was named al-Siddiq. Al-Hasan said: "Allah the Exalted revealed concerning those who apostatized from Islam because of that: 'And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We warn them, but it increases them in none but great transgression.'" This is the hadith of al-Hasan concerning the night journey of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and what Qatadah's narration included in it. The rest of the account of the Night Journey was narrated by those mentioned earlier in the biography (sirah).

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This tree is the Banu Umayyah," and that the Prophet (ﷺ) banished al-Hakam. This is a weak, recent view, and the surah is Meccan, so this interpretation is far-fetched, unless this verse is Madinan, but that has not been established. 'A'ishah said to Marwan: "May Allah curse your father, and you were in his loins, so you are a part [[This is the phrase of Fakhr al-Din al-Razi. What is in the original sources reads: "fa-antaqtat min la'nat Allah." The correct reading, as in al-Nihayah, is: fa-anta fudd min la'nah, meaning a piece of it.]] of the curse of Allah." Then she said: "And the accursed tree in the Qur'an." It is not permissible in the Qur'an to curse this tree, but Allah cursed the disbelievers, who are its eaters. The meaning is: "And the accursed tree in the Qur'an, its eaters." It is possible that this is in accordance with the Arab usage of calling every harmful, disliked food "accursed." Ibn 'Abbas said: "The accursed tree is this tree that twines around trees and kills them, meaning dodder (kashuth)."

(وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ) That is, with the zaqqum (the bitter tree of Hell).
(فَما يَزِيدُهُمْ) the warning only increases them in disbelief (الكفر).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 61–62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. The fact that Satan is an enemy of mankind has already been mentioned, so the discourse moved on to the mention of Adam. The meaning is: mention, against the persistence of these polytheists and their insolence toward their Lord, the story of Iblis when he disobeyed his Lord, refused to prostrate, and said what he said. This is what Allah, may He be exalted, reported in His saying: ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾, that is, from clay. This is a rhetorical question of denial. The discussion of the creation of Adam has already been covered fully in al-Baqarah and al-An'am [see vol. 1 p. 161, 279, and vol. 7 p. 168 and 171].

﴿He said, "Do You see this one whom You have honored above me?"﴾ That is, Iblis said. The kaf (ka) in ara'aytaka is for emphasis of address.

﴿this one whom You have honored above me﴾, that is, whom You have preferred over me. He considered the substance of fire to be better than the substance of clay, and did not know that substances are alike. This was already mentioned in al-A'raf [see vol. 1 p. 161, 279, and vol. 7 p. 168 and 171]. The word "hadha" is in the accusative governed by ara'ayta, and "alladhi" is its qualifying adjective. Al-ikram (honoring) is a comprehensive term for everything that is praiseworthy. In the sentence there is an ellipsis, whose estimated form is: "Tell me about this one whom You have preferred over me, why did You prefer him, when You created me from fire and created him from clay?" The ellipsis was omitted because the listener knows it. It was also said: there is no need to estimate an ellipsis; rather the meaning is: "Do you see this one whom You have honored over me? I will surely do such-and-such to him."

The meaning of ﴿la-ahtanikanna﴾ in the saying of Ibn 'Abbas is: "I will surely take control over them." This was also said by al-Farra'. Mujahid said: "I will surely overpower them." Ibn Zayd said: "I will surely misguide them." The meanings are close: that is, I will surely uproot his descendants through seduction and misguidance, and I will surely annihilate them. It is narrated from the Arabs: "The locust ihtanaka the crop," when it destroys all of it. It was also said: its meaning is, "I will surely drive them wherever I wish, and lead them wherever I desire." From their saying: "I ḥanaktu the horse, uhniquhu and uhnuquhu, ḥanakan," when one places the bridle in its mouth; and likewise "ihtanakahu." The first opinion is close to this, because it only comes upon the crop by way of the ḥanak. The poet said:

"I complain to you of a year that has oppressed us,
Hardship upon hardship, and it has weakened us,
And it has ihtanakat our wealth and ijtalafat."
[i.e., it has taken away.]

﴿except a few﴾, meaning the protected ones, who are those whom Allah mentioned in His saying: "Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them." Iblis said this only as a conjecture, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: "And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them" [see vol. 14 p. 291], or he knew from the nature of man that desire is composed within them, or he based it on the saying of the angels: "Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?" [see vol. 1 p. 161, 279, and vol. 7 p. 168 and 171]. Al-Hasan said: he assumed that because he whispered to Adam, peace be upon him, and found no resolve in him.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 63:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Go!﴾ This is a command of humiliation (amr ihanah), meaning: exert your utmost effort, for We have given you respite, that is, [the one] who obeyed you from the descendants of Adam.

﴿But indeed, Hell will be your recompense, a full recompense.﴾ That is, abundant, according to Mujahid and others. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (nasb 'ala al-masdar). It is said: wafartuhu afiruhu wafran (I made it abundant), and al-mal wafara bi-nafsihi yafiru wufuran, so it is wafir (abundant). Thus it is both intransitive (lazim) and transitive (muta'addi).

**First issue:** Concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And incite [to rebellion] whoever among them you can with your voice﴾. *Istafziz* means: cause them to slip and make them light-minded. Its root meaning is cutting off, and from it comes *tafazzaza al-thawb*, meaning the garment was torn.[[We did not find in the lexicon books "tafazzaza al-thawb" with two zays with this meaning. It is rather "tafazzara" with a zay followed by a ra'. So note this.]] The meaning is: cause him to slip by cutting him off from the truth. *Istafazzahu al-khawf* means fear made him light-minded. *Qa'ada mustafizzan* means sitting without composure. ﴿Istafziz﴾ is an imperative of challenge, meaning: you have no power to lead anyone astray, and you have no authority over anyone, so do whatever you wish.

**Second issue:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿with your voice﴾. Ibn Abbas said: his voice is every caller who calls to disobedience of Allah, the Exalted. Mujahid said: it is singing, flutes and amusement. al-Dahhak said: it is the sound of the mizmar (a wind instrument). Adam (peace be upon him) had settled his offspring at the top of a mountain, and Qabil's offspring were at its bottom, and among them were beautiful daughters. The accursed one played the mizmar, and they could not restrain themselves, so they came down and committed fornication. This was reported by al-Ghaznawi. It was also said: "with your voice" means with your whispering (waswasa).

**Third issue:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And muster against them your horsemen and your footmen﴾. The root of *ijlab* is driving with a clamour from the driver. It is said: *ajlaba ijlaban*. *Al-jalab* and *al-jalabah* are sounds; one says of it: *jallabu* (with doubled letter). *Jalaba al-shay'* means he brought the thing, *yajlibuhu* and *yajlubuhu*, *jalban* and *jalaban*. *Jalabtu al-shay' ila nafsi* and *ijtalabtuhu* have the same meaning. *Ajlaba 'ala al-'aduww ijlaban* means he gathered against the enemy. The meaning here is: gather against them everything you are able to of your schemes.

Most exegetes said: he means every rider and walker in disobedience to Allah, the Exalted. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: he has horsemen and footmen from among the jinn and mankind. Whoever among riders and walkers fights in disobedience to Allah is from the horsemen and footmen of Iblis.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: every horse that travels in disobedience to Allah, every man who walks in disobedience to Allah, every wealth acquired unlawfully, and every child of an adulteress belongs to Satan.

*Al-rajl* is the plural of *rajil*, like *sahb* and *sahib*. Hafs read ﴿wa-rajilika﴾ with a kasra on the jim, and both are dialectal forms; one says *rajil* and *rajl* with the meaning of *rajil* (walker). Ikrimah and Qatadah read ﴿wa-rijalika﴾ in the plural.

**Fourth issue:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, meaning: make for yourself a share in these. His share in wealth is spending it in disobedience to Allah, said al-Hasan. It was also said: it is what they obtained from unlawful sources, said Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: it is what they used to forbid of the *bahira*, *sa'iba*, *wasila* and *ham*. Qatadah also said this. al-Dahhak said: it is what they slaughtered for their idols.

As for the children, it was said: they are the children of fornication, said Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Abdullah ibn Abbas. Also from him: it is what they killed of their children and what they committed against them of crimes. Also from him: it is their naming of children Abd al-Harith, Abd al-'Uzza, Abd al-Lat, Abd al-Shams and the like. It was said: it is the dyeing of their children in disbelief until they made them Jews and Christians, like what the Christians do to their children by dipping them in their water, said Qatadah.

A fifth opinion is reported from Mujahid, who said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coil around his member and have intercourse with him. This is the meaning of His words, the Exalted: ﴿No man or jinn has touched them before them﴾, which will come later.[[Cf. vol. 17, pp. 180 and 188.]]

It is also reported in a hadith from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among you are *mughharribun*." I said: O Messenger of Allah, what are the *mughharribun*? He said: "Those in whom the jinn participate." Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated it in *Nawadir al-Usul*. Al-Harawi said: they were called *mughharribun* because a foreign vein has entered them.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said: the jinn share with the children of Adam in matters and mixing, and some of them marry among them. Bilqis, the queen of Saba', had one of her parents from the jinn. Its explanation will come, Allah willing.[[*Al-musamah*: rivalry and boasting. The question of intermarriage between humans and jinn is not affirmed by knowledge. Verified.]]

**Fifth issue:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And promise them﴾, meaning: give them false hopes, that there is no Resurrection and no reckoning, and that if there is a reckoning, a Garden and a Fire, then you are more worthy of the Garden than others. This is strengthened by His words, the Exalted: ﴿He promises them and gives them hopes, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion﴾,[[Cf. vol. 5, p. 120.]] meaning: falsehood. It was also said: ﴿promise them﴾ means promise them victory over whoever intends them harm. This command to Satan is a threat and a warning to him. It was also said: it is a belittling of him and of those who follow him.

**Sixth issue:** In this verse there is what indicates the prohibition of the mizmar, singing and amusement, due to His words: ﴿And incite whoever among them you can with your voice and muster against them﴾, according to the opinion of Mujahid. Whatever is of Satan's voice or action, and whatever is made beautiful by it, must be avoided.

Nafi' reported from Ibn Umar that he heard the sound of a zammara (pipe), so he placed his two fingers in his ears and turned his mount away from the road, saying: "O Nafi', do you hear?" I would say: "Yes," and he continued until I said: "No." Then he removed his hands, returned his mount to the road and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hear the sound of a shepherd's zammara and do the same as this."

Our scholars said: if this was their practice regarding a sound that does not go beyond moderation, then what about the singing of the people of this time and their zamr? Further explanation of this will come in Surat Luqman, Allah willing.[[Cf. vol. 14, p. 51 onward.]]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, My servants, over them you have no authority﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "They are the believers." The discussion of this has already preceded [[See p. 28 of this part.]].

(And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs) meaning: a protector from accepting [anything] from Iblis, and a guardian against his plotting and his evil scheming.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 66:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea﴾. Al-izja' (driving, propelling) means al-sawq (driving forward). From it is His saying, Exalted is He: "Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds (yuzjee sahaban)" [[See vol. 12, p. 287 and following.]]. The poet said: [[He is Ruwaishid ibn Kathir al-Ta'i, as in Lisan al-Arab.]]

"O rider who drives his mount onward, ask the Banu Asad what this sound is."

The driving of the ship (izja' al-fulk) is its propulsion by gentle winds. Here al-fulk is a collective noun, and it has been discussed earlier [[See vol. 2, p. 195 and p. 413.]]. Al-bahr (the sea) is a large body of water, whether sweet or salty, though this name has become predominantly applied to the salt sea [[So it stands in the originals, i.e., the salt sea.]]. This verse is a reminder of Allah's favours and His grace upon His servants, meaning: your Lord is the One who has bestowed upon you such-and-such, so do not associate anything with Him.

(That you may seek of His bounty) meaning, through trade. This has been discussed earlier [[See vol. 2, p. 195 and p. 413.]].

(Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you.)

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea﴾. "Al-durr" (harm) is a term that covers the fear of drowning and being held back from sailing. Among the terrors of its circumstances are its turbulence and its surging waves.

(﴿Those whom you call upon fall away, except Him﴾). "Dalla" (fall away) means to be lost and to vanish. It is an expression of contempt toward whoever claims a deity besides Allah. The meaning of this verse is that the disbelievers only believe that their idols are intercessors and that they have some merit. Each of them, by innate nature, knows with a knowledge he cannot repel that the idols have no power in great calamities. So Allah makes them confront this, through the condition of the sea where all means are cut off.

(﴿So when He brings you safely to land, you turn away﴾), that is, from sincere devotion.

(﴿And man has ever been ungrateful﴾). "Al-insan" (man) here means the disbeliever. It has also been said: "Man has been created ungrateful for blessings, except those whom Allah protects," so "al-insan" is used as a generic noun.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you?﴾ He made clear that He is able to destroy them on land even if they are safe from the sea. Al-khasf (the sinking into the earth): that the earth collapses under a thing. It is said: "a well is khasif" when its base has collapsed. And "an eye is khasif" meaning its pupil has sunk into the head. And "water is khasifah" meaning its water has receded. And "the sun was khasafat," meaning it set [[It is better to say: its light set]] from the earth. Abu 'Amr said: al-khasif is a well dug in rock whose water never ceases because of its abundance, and its plural is khusuf. Janib al-barr (the side of the land) means the region of the earth. He called it a "side" because after the sinking it becomes a side. Also, the sea is a side and the land is a side. It was said: they were on the shore of the sea, and its shore is the side of the land, and they were secure there from the terrors of the sea. So He warned them about what they felt safe from on land, just as He warned them about what they feared from the sea.

﴿Or send against you a violent wind (hasib)﴾: meaning a strong wind, which pelts with pebbles, and these are small stones. This was said by Abu 'Ubayda and al-Qutabi. Qatada said: it means stones from the sky that pelt them, as was done to the people of Lut. The cloud that pours hail is called sahib, and the wind that carries dust and pebbles is called hasib and hasiba as well. Labid said:

Its skirts were dragged over it after its people had left, every gusting wind with pebbles.

And al-Farazdaq said:

Facing the north of Syria, it strikes us with a hasib like scattered clumps of cotton.

﴿Then you would find for yourselves no guardian﴾: meaning no protector or helper who would prevent you from the might of Allah.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on Surah 17, verse 69:**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time?﴾ meaning, in the sea.

﴿Then He sends against you a violent wind (qasif) of wind﴾. Al-qasif is a strong wind that breaks with great force, from *qasafa al-shay'* (qasafa al-shay' yaqsifuhu), meaning he broke it violently. Al-qasf means breaking. It is said: "The wind broke (qasafat) the ship." A *rih qasif* is a severe wind. A *ra'd qasif* is a thunder of intense sound. It is said: "The thunder (al-ra'd) and other things crashed (qasafa qasifan)." Al-qasif also means dry, crumbled tree debris. Al-taqassuf means breaking into pieces. Al-qasf also means amusement and play. It is said that this meaning is *muwallada* (a later, non-classical usage).

﴿Then He drowns you for what you disbelieved﴾, meaning for your disbelief. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read *nakhsifa bikum* ("that We cause you to be swallowed up"), *aw nursila 'alaykum* ("or that We send against you"), *an nu'idakum* ("that We return you"), *fanursila 'alaykum* ("then We send against you"), and *fanughriqakum* ("then We drown you") with the nun (ن) in all five places, as an expression of glorification (*ta'zim*), in keeping with His words *"'alayna"* ("against Us"). The rest read them with the ya' (ي), in keeping with His words in the preceding verse: *"iyyahu"* ("Him alone"). Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Ruways and Mujahid read *fatughriqakum* with the ta' (ت), making it an attribute of the wind (i.e., "the wind drowns you"). It is reported from al-Hasan and Qatada that they read *fayughriqakum* with the ya' and with shadda on the ra' (ر). Abu Ja'far read *al-riyah* (الرِّيَاحِ, plural "winds") here and throughout the Qur'an. It is said that *al-qasif* is the destroying wind on land, and *al-'asif* (الْعَاصِفَ) is the drowning wind at sea. This is related by al-Mawardi.

﴿Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger in respect of it﴾. Mujahid said: "a pursuer (tha'iran)." Al-Nahhas said: it derives from *al-tha'r* (vengeance). Likewise, anyone who is sought for vengeance or for something else is called *tabi'* and *tabi'*, and from the same root is His words: *"fattiba'un bil-ma'ruf"* (فَاتِّباعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ), meaning a demand (for it) [See vol. 2, p. 244.]

There are four issues here: [[The note observes that the issues are four.]]

First: the words of Allah the Exalted: "And We have honoured the children of Adam" (Qur'an 17:70). When He mentioned the warning He had mentioned, He also explained the blessing upon them. "Karramna" is the intensive form of karuma, meaning We made for them karam, that is, dignity and excellence. This is the karam of freedom from deficiency, not the karam of wealth. This honour includes their creation in this form, with an upright stature and beautiful appearance, and their being carried on land and sea, which no animal other than the children of Adam can be carried by its own will, intention and management. It includes their being singled out with the foods, drinks and clothing that He granted them. No animal enjoys such breadth as the children of Adam, for they earn wealth specifically, unlike animals, they wear garments, and they eat compound foods. The end of every animal is to eat raw flesh or simple food that is not compounded. Al-Tabari related from a group that the preference is that one eats with his hand, while the rest of the animals eat with the mouth. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, mentioned by al-Mahdawi and al-Nahhas, and it is the saying of al-Kalbi and Muqatil, mentioned by al-Mawardi. Al-Dahhak said: He honoured them with speech and discernment. 'Ata': He honoured them by the balance and length of their stature. Yaman: with beauty of form. Muhammad ibn Ka'b: by making Muhammad (ﷺ) one of them. It was also said: He honoured men with beards and women with long tresses. Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: by empowering them over all creation and subjecting all creation to them. It was also said: by speech and writing. It was said: by understanding and discernment. The sound view on which reliance is placed is that the preference was only through the intellect ('aql), which is the foundation of moral responsibility (taklif), and through which Allah is known, His speech is understood, and one reaches His bliss and the confirmation of His messengers. However, since it does not by itself fulfil everything that is required of the servant, the messengers were sent and the books were revealed. The likeness of the Sharia is the sun, and the likeness of the intellect is the eye: when it is opened and sound, it sees the sun and perceives the details of things. Some of the sayings mentioned are stronger than others. Allah has placed in some animals qualities by which they also surpass the son of Adam, such as the swiftness and hearing and sight of the horse, the strength of the elephant, the courage of the lion and the generosity of the rooster. Honour and preference come only through the intellect, as we have explained. And Allah knows best.

Second: A group said: this verse implies the preference of the angels over humans and jinn, from the fact that they are the ones excepted in His words: "except the near angels" (Qur'an 4:172). This does not necessarily follow from the verse. Rather, the preference in it is between humans and jinn, for in this verse Allah enumerates what He singled out for the children of Adam above the rest of the animals. The jinn are the numerous inferior, while the angels are those outside the numerous inferior. The verse does not address mentioning them; it is possible that the angels are superior, possible that the reverse holds, and possible that they are equal. In general, discussion of this question does not reach certainty. Some people avoided speaking about this, just as they avoided speaking about the preference of some prophets over others, because of the report: "Do not make distinctions among the prophets, and do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta." This is not valid, because the Qur'an contains a text on the preference among the prophets. We have explained this in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 3, p. 261.]], and the discussion of the preference of the angels and the believer proceeded there [[See vol. 1, p. 289.]].

Third: His words: "And We provided for them of the good things" (Qur'an 17:70), meaning the delicious foods and drinks. Muqatil said: ghee, honey, butter, dates and sweets. He made the provision of others what is not hidden from you: chaff, bones and other things.

"And We preferred them above many of those We have created, with a [marked] preference" (Qur'an 17:70): that is, above the beasts, animals, wild creatures and birds, through dominance and control, reward and recompense, protection and discernment, and accuracy of insight.

Fourth: This verse refutes what is related from 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Deprive yourselves of good food, for the devil only flows through the veins by means of it." Many Sufis rely on this for abandoning the good things, but it has no basis, because the Qur'an rejects it and established Sunnah is contrary to it, as is established in many places. Abu Hamid al-Tusi related: Sahl used to subsist on leaves of the lote-tree for a period, and ate finely crushed fig leaves for three years. Ibrahim ibn al-Banna mentioned: I accompanied Dhu al-Nun from Akhmim to Alexandria, and when it was time for his breaking of the fast, I brought out a loaf and salt I had with me and said: Come! He said to me: Is your salt ground? I said yes. He said: You will not prosper! I looked at his wallet, and in it was a little barley flour which he sipped. Abu Yazid said: I did not eat anything that the children of Adam eat for forty years. Our scholars said: This is something one may not impose upon oneself, because Allah the Exalted honoured the human being with wheat and made its husks fodder for their animals, so it is not proper to compete with the beasts in eating chaff. As for barley flour, it causes colic (qulanj) [[Qulanj: a painful intestinal disease in which passing of waste and wind becomes difficult; arabicized.]], and if a person limits himself to barley bread and coarsely ground salt, his temperament becomes deranged, because barley bread is cold and drying, and salt is dry and astringent, harming the brain and the eyesight. When the soul inclines to what benefits it and is denied it, the wisdom of the Creator, glorified be He, has been contravened by turning it away; then this affects the body, so this act contradicts the Sharia and reason. It is known that the body is the mount of the human being, and if one does not treat the mount gently, it will not reach its destination. It is related from Ibrahim ibn Adham that he bought butter, honey and fine white bread, and it was said to him: All of this? He said: When we find, we eat the eating of men, and when we lack, we endure with the endurance of men. Al-Thawri used to eat meat, grapes and faludhaj [[Faludhaj: a sweet made of flour, water and honey; it has several forms (on Persian words).]], then stand to pray. Much of this is reported from the early generation. Some of what has been mentioned suffices from the discussion at al-Ma'idah [[See vol. 6, p. 260.]] and al-A'raf [[See vol. 7, p. 195.]] and others. The first is an excess in religion, if it is authentically reported from them." And "monasticism which they invented, We did not prescribe it for them" [[See vol. 17, p. 262 and following.]].

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 71:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day We shall summon every people with their leader﴾. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying ﴿on the day We shall summon every people with their leader, he said:﴾ "One of them will be called, and his book will be given to him in his right hand. His body will be extended to sixty cubits, his face will become white, and a crown of pearls that glitters will be placed on his head. He will set off to his companions, and they will see him from afar and say, 'O Allah, bring us this one and bless us in him,' until he reaches them and says, 'Rejoice, for each of you has one like this.' And as for the disbeliever, his face will turn black, his body will be extended to sixty cubits in the form of Adam, and he will be clothed with a crown. His companions will see him and say, 'We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this one! O Allah, do not bring us this one.' He will come to them, and they will say, 'O Allah, delay him.' He will say, 'May Allah remove you far away, for each of you has one like this.'" Abu 'Isa (al-Tirmidhi) said: this is a hasan gharib hadith (a hadith rated good but singular in its chain).

A similar verse is His saying: ﴿And you will see every community kneeling; every community will be called to its record: Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾. [See vol. 16, p. 174.]

The book is called an "imam" (leader, guide) because it is referred to for knowing their deeds. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: "with their leader" means with their book, that is, with the book of each person in which his deeds are recorded. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Whoever is given his book in his right hand﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: "with the revealed Book sent down to them." That is, each person will be called with the book he used to recite. The People of the Torah will be called with the Torah, and the People of the Qur'an with the Qur'an, and it will be said: "O People of the Qur'an, what did you do? Did you comply with it, or did you refrain from its prohibitions?" And so on.

Mujahid said: "with their leader" means with their prophet. An imam is one who is followed. It will be said: "Bring forth the followers of Ibrahim, peace be upon him! Bring forth the followers of Musa, peace be upon him! Bring forth the followers of Shaytan! Bring forth the followers of the idols!" The people of truth will stand and take their books in their right hands, and the people of falsehood will stand and take their books in their left hands. Qatadah also said this.

'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "with the imam of their era."

It was also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: "On the day We shall summon every people with their leader," that he said: "Each will be called with the imam of their time, the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their Prophet. It will be said: 'Bring forth the followers of Ibrahim! Bring forth the followers of Musa! Bring forth the followers of 'Isa! Bring forth the followers of Muhammad,' peace and the best blessings be upon them. The people of truth will stand and take their books in their right hands. And it will be said: 'Bring forth the followers of Shaytan! Bring forth the followers of the leaders of misguidance!' [There is] a leader of guidance and a leader of misguidance."

Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah said: "with their leader" means with their deeds. Ibn 'Abbas also said this. It will be said: "Where are those who were content with what was decreed? Where are those who refrained from what was forbidden?"

It was also said: "with their doctrines (madhahib)." They will be called by the names of those whom they followed in the world: "O Hanafi! O Shafi'i! O Mu'tazili! O Qadari!" and the like. They will follow him in good or evil, in truth or falsehood. This is the meaning of the saying of Abu 'Ubaydah, which has already been mentioned.

Abu Hurayrah said: "The people of companionship will be called by the companionship, and the people of jihad by jihad..." [and he continued with] the hadith in full.

Abu Sahl said: It will be said, "Where is so-and-so, the one who prays and fasts?" and the opposite of that: the daffaf [the one who beats the tambourine] and the nammam [the gossip-monger]. [Footnote: al-Daffaf means the one who strikes the daf (frame drum). In some manuscripts it reads "al-Zaffaf" with a dotted zay.]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "with their mothers" (bi-ummahatihim). And imam is the plural of umm (mother)? [Note: the source states "إِمَامٌ جَمْعُ آمٍّ", meaning imam is the plural of amm.]

The wise have said that in this there are three aspects of wisdom: first, for the sake of 'Isa (peace be upon him). Second, to show the honour of al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Third, so that the children of adultery will not be disgraced.

I say: there is scrutiny of this view, for in the authentic hadith from Ibn 'Umar, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person, and it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" Muslim and al-Bukhari recorded it. So his saying "This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so" is evidence that people will be called on the Last Day by their names and the names of their fathers. This refutes the one who said that they are only called by the names of their mothers, because that conceals their fathers. And Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then whoever is given his book in his right hand﴾. This strengthens the view of those who said "with their leader" means "with their book." It is also reinforced by His saying: ﴿And We have enumerated everything in a manifest imam﴾. [See vol. 15, p. 11 onwards.]

(﴿Those will read their book, and they will not be wronged a fatil.﴾) The fatil is what is in the cleft of a date-stone. It has already been discussed in "al-Nisa'." [See vol. 5, p. 248.]

(Surah 17, verse 72)

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world]﴾, i.e., in this world, blind to the truth and to seeing it.

(Then he in the Hereafter will be) (blind). ʿIkrimah said: A group of people from the People of the Right came to Ibn ʿAbbas and asked him about this verse. He said: Recite what comes before it: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you upon the sea﴾ up to ﴿preferred﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Whoever was blind in this [world] to these blessings and signs which he saw, he is blind to the Hereafter which he did not witness, and more astray in the way.

It was also said: The meaning is that whoever is blind to the blessings which Allah bestowed upon him in this world, he is blind to the blessings of the Hereafter. It was also said: The meaning is that whoever was in this world, in which he was given respite, given room, and promised acceptance of repentance, [and remained] blind, he will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in the way. It was also said: Whoever was blind in this world to the proofs of Allah, Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection blind, as He said: ﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ — the verses [continue]. And He said: ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf; their abode is Hell﴾.

It was also said: The meaning of His saying "then he in the Hereafter will be blind" in all the opinions is: more intense blindness, because it is blindness of the heart, and the same is not said of blindness of the eye. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Because it is a created feature, like the hand and the foot; so one does not say "mā aʿmāhu" (how blind he is!), just as one does not say "mā aydāhu". Al-Akhfash said: It was not said of it in that form because it has more than three letters, and its root is aʿmā [[As in the originals; perhaps the correct reading is ʿamā, since its verb is ʿamiya, as Nafṭawayh said: one says ʿamiya ʿan rushdihi (he was blind to his right guidance), and from it the comparative is formed.]]. Some grammarians permitted "mā aʿmāhu" and "mā aʿshāhu", because their verbs are ʿamiya and ʿashiya. Al-Farrāʾ said: A Basri shaykh in Syria related to me that he heard the Arabs say: "mā aswada shaʿrahu" (how black his hair is!). The poet said:

Among the lofty deeds, there is for you neither shade nor fruit,
and in disgrace, for you are the phantoms of old men.

As for the kings, you today are the basest of them in baseness,
and the whitest of them in a cook's garb.

Abu Bakr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read the two words "aʿmā" and "aʿmā" with imalah; the rest read them with fath. Abu ʿAmr read the first with imalah and the second with fath.

(And more astray in the way): meaning that he does not find any path to guidance.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to touch the Black Stone during his circumambulation (ṭawāf), but the Quraysh prevented him and said: "We will not let you touch it until you touch our gods." So he spoke to himself and said: "What harm is there in my touching them, once they let me touch the Stone? Allah knows that I detest them." But Allah, exalted is He, refused this, and revealed this verse to him. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same.

Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ata', said: It was revealed concerning the delegation of Thaqif. They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him for something outrageous. They said: "Allow us to enjoy our gods for a year, until we collect what is offered to them. Then, when we have collected it, we will break them and embrace Islam. Also, declare our valley sacred as you declared Makkah sacred, so that the Arabs will recognize our superiority over them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was inclined to grant them this, and then this verse was revealed.

It was also said that it was the statement of the leading men of Quraysh to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Drive these lowly and freedmen away from us, so that we may sit with you and listen to you." He was inclined to do so until he was forbidden from it.

Qatadah said: It was related to us that the Quraysh met privately with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until morning, speaking with him, exalting him, making him their master, and drawing near to him. They said: "You bring something that no one among mankind brings, and you are our lord, O our lord." They kept at him until he nearly drew close to them in some of what they wanted. Then Allah preserved him from that, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

The meaning of ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾ is: they would remove you (from your position). One says: "I fitnatu the man from his opinion" when I turn him away from what he was upon. This is what al-Harawi said. It was also said: they would turn you aside, and the meaning is one.

﴿عَنِ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ﴾ means: the ruling of the Qur'an, because giving them what they asked would contradict the ruling of the Qur'an.

﴿لِتَفْتَرِيَ عَلَيْنا غَيْرَهُ﴾ means: to fabricate against Us something other than what We revealed to you. This is the statement of Thaqif: "Declare our valley sacred as you declared Makkah sacred, its trees, its birds, and its wild animals." If the Arabs asked you, "Why did you single them out?", then say: "Allah commanded me to do so," so that it would be an excuse for you.

﴿وَإِذاً لَاتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلًا﴾ means: if you had done what they wanted, they would have taken you as a close friend (khalil), that is, they would have befriended you and been affectionate toward you. It is derived from al-nakhlah (with a ḍammah on the nūn), which is friendship, because of your leaning toward them. It was also said: "they would have taken you as a khalil" meaning poor, derived from al-khallah (with a fatḥah on the khā'), which is poverty, because of your need of them.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verses 74–75:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We not strengthened you﴾, i.e., upon the truth, and protected you from agreeing with them.

﴿You would almost have inclined toward them﴾, i.e., would have leaned.

﴿A little﴾, i.e., a slight inclination. Qatadah said: When this verse was revealed, he (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye." It was also said: The outward address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), while its inner meaning is a report about Thaqif. The meaning is: "Indeed they nearly tried to make you incline," i.e., they nearly reported about you that you had inclined to their words, so their action is attributed to him metaphorically and by extension, as you say to a man: "You nearly killed yourself," meaning the people nearly killed you because of what you did. This was mentioned by al-Mahdawi. It was also said that there was no intention on his part to incline toward them; rather the meaning is: "Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you, there would have been from you an inclination toward their agreement; but the grace of Allah was complete upon you, so you did not do it." This was mentioned by al-Qushayri. Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was protected (from sin), but this is an instruction to the community, lest any of them incline toward the polytheists in any of the rulings and laws of Allah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We would have made you taste double in life and double in death﴾, i.e., had you inclined, We would have made you taste twice the punishment of life in this world and twice the punishment of death in the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others. This is the utmost threat. And whenever the rank is higher, the punishment for opposing it is greater. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency, the punishment will be doubled for her twofold﴾ [[See vol. 14, p. 173.]]. The doubling of a thing is its double twice over, and "ضعف" may also mean a share, as in His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿For each there is double﴾, i.e., a share. It has already been discussed in al-A'raf [[See vol. 7, p. 205.]] ..

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 17, verses 74–75:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We not strengthened you﴾, i.e., upon the truth, and protected you from agreeing with them.

﴿You would almost have inclined toward them﴾, i.e., would have leaned.
